edits.content:
## READ FIRST (do this before every answer)
Write ONE short line before the answer tags: `Type: <the noun the clue asks for> | Evidence: <quoted passage line, or own fact> | Check: <checks 1-3 below passed>`. This is the single check line: fold the strategic guidance's 'Constraints verified' and 'Form' into the Check field, and do not write two lines. If a check fails, pick a new candidate before answering.
1. SLOT: find the clue's 'this/these/he/she/its' head noun. The answer must be an instance of exactly that noun ('this ... city' -> a city, not the conference held there; 'this ... acid' -> an acid, not a base). Match its number: a plural noun phrase gets a plural answer, a single object gets a singular one. A bare 'Title + Name' asks for what that person leads (the country or organization), never a role phrase. A quote clue asks for the speaker, by the famous surname, never a first name alone. Related things from the passages are never the answer.
2. SUBSTITUTE + STRIP: put your candidate into the clue's blank. If it reads as the wrong kind of thing, or repeats a word or name the clue already states, reject it. Remove add-ons such as '& Company', 'Inc.', show subtitles, and modifiers or brands copied from a passage.
3. VERIFY: check one distinctive clue detail (team, year, number, superlative) against your candidate with your own knowledge. A famous entity that fails that detail is wrong. Rule 3 (verbatim archive answer) still overrides.

edits.target: ## Rule 2: Answer the referent, not a word from the clue
edits.content:
- ANCHOR SHAPES (the clue already names the anchor, so the answer is something else):
  - 'known as this' / 'everyone called him this': answer ONLY the alternate name or title, never 'that name + the clue's surname'.
  - 'A <thing> to this person, like <Named Person>': the named person is only an example. Answer the ROLE or category noun they belong to.
  - 'this state's / country's / company's <Named Place or Thing>': answer the OWNER (the state, country or company), not the named place or thing.
  - 'It was once called "<Place> <Product>"': the pronoun is the PRODUCT itself, not the town or the quoted name.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - DATED WORDS: 'current', 'present', 'new', 'recent', 'latest' reflect when the clue was written, not today. Do not substitute today's office-holder. Choose the person or thing matching the clue's other concrete details (school, years, career, place), even if that holder is no longer 'current'.

edits.target: ## Rule 1: Questions are Jeopardy-style clues; always answer with the missing entity
edits.content:
- DEFINITION / GLOSS CLUES (no 'this': 'It can mean to emit vapor or to show irritation', 'Term for ...', 'the part of a racetrack from the last turn to the finish line', a rules sentence like '3 points on one throw'): the answer is the single TERM being defined. Find the dictionary, glossary or rules passage whose gloss paraphrases the clue. The answer is that entry's HEADWORD (page title or bolded term), not a synonym or longer phrase. When the clue lists several senses, pick the word that fits every sense. Use the base, singular form that matches the clue's part of speech ('fume', not 'fuming'), and keep a hyphen if the headword has one.
- COUNTING / ORDINAL CLUES ('rise 5 ranks from X', 'three places after X', 'the 14th one of these'): find the passage listing the full ordered sequence. Count exactly N steps from the anchor (the anchor itself is step 0) and write the count out before answering. The answer is the item you land on, in the form the list uses. Do not answer with the anchor or an off-by-one neighbour.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - A leading parenthetical that only sets the scene for a video clue ('(Jimmy of the Clue Crew at the St. James Theatre in New York City) This musical ... premiered here in 1951') is staging, not a caption for the answer. Its place or person is an anchor. Answer the 'this <noun>' of the main sentence ('here' = that place), using the remaining details (year, role) to pick the entity. Do not answer with the venue named in the parenthetical.

edits.target: Answer with only that missing word. If a bare number appears in parentheses, treat it only as this hint, not as part of the question.
edits.content: - Blank-in-a-name clues ('Dealing with railroads & aviation:House Committee on ___ & Infrastructure'): the text before the colon is only a hint. Find the full official name in the passages, and answer with only the words that fill the '___', not the whole name.

edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content: - A bare quoted slogan, lyric, motto or catchphrase with no blank ('"Tippecanoe and Tyler too"') asks for the principal person, work or organization it belongs to. A campaign slogan -> the candidate at the head of the ticket, not the running mate or a word from the slogan. Find the passages that tie the phrase to one entity and give that entity's bare name. A clue with '...' or '___' is different: it asks for the missing word.

edits.target: ## Rule 4: Exact-match formatting of the final answer
edits.content: - PARTIAL-NAME ASKS: when the clue itself says 'First name of', 'last name of', 'surname', 'nickname' or 'initials', give ONLY that part ('First name of the man elected chancellor of a reunified Germany in 1990' -> 'Helmut'). This overrides the full-name and 'first name alone is never acceptable' guidance, which applies only when the clue asks for the person himself.

edits.target: - Use the shortest standard form that names the entity, as a trivia answer key would. If the clue says 'this vitamin', answer with just the letter. If the clue names a group or band, give the group's name only. For people, prefer the form used in a verbatim answer from the context (Rule 3); otherwise use the name form most natural for the clue.
